meta.title: Konechi — see whether you are on ethernet or Wi-Fi
meta.description: A tiny Mac app that keeps whether you are on a cable or on Wi-Fi visible in the menu bar.

hero.tagline: Cable or Wi-Fi, at a glance
hero.lead: You plugged the cable in, but you are still on Wi-Fi — and nothing on screen tells you. Konechi keeps the connection you are actually using visible in your menu bar.

states.title: She reacts to your connection
states.lead: On top form with a cable, doing fine on Wi-Fi, out of energy when nothing is connected.

truth.title: Switches the moment you plug in
truth.body: Having a cable in while Wi-Fi is still on is normal, and only one of them is carrying your traffic. Konechi asks the Mac itself which one that is, and her face changes the instant you plug in or pull out.

details.title: Speed and traffic, one click away
details.body: Click the icon and you get the name of what you are connected to, the IP address, how fast the link is, and how much is flowing right now. Useful when something feels slow and you want to know how far it gets.

vpn.title: Still visible through a VPN
vpn.body: Turn a VPN on and most apps lose sight of the connection underneath. Konechi adds a padlock and keeps showing whether the cable or Wi-Fi is doing the work behind it.

quiet.title: Just leave it there
quiet.body: No dock icon, no window, no account. All you decide is whether it starts with your Mac and which rows you want to see.

install.title: One extra step the first time
install.body: The author is not a registered Apple developer, so the first launch says the developer cannot be verified. Open System Settings, go to Privacy & Security, and click Open Anyway. After that it behaves like any other app.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Konechi looks at how your Mac is connected and puts a mark in the menu bar. That's the whole app. It has no server, no analytics, and no account.

sections.title: What it reads
sections.body: Konechi asks macOS which network route is currently active and what the interfaces on the machine are called, which is enough to tell Ethernet from Wi-Fi and to show the name of the connection. It reads configuration, not traffic — it does not see, log, or touch anything you send or receive.

sections.title: Nothing leaves the Mac
sections.body: What it reads is used to draw a mark in the menu bar and is not stored, collected, or uploaded. There is nowhere for it to be uploaded to.

sections.title: Update checks go to GitHub
sections.body: Konechi checks for a new version once when it starts, not on a timer. The check fetches a small file from its GitHub Releases page, so GitHub sees the request the way it sees any download, including your IP address. It is a plain file download and carries nothing about your network.

sections.title: No analytics, ever
sections.body: There is no crash reporting, no usage tracking, no unique identifier, and no third-party SDK of any kind in the app.

sections.title: You can check all of this
sections.body: Konechi is open source under the MIT license, so none of the above has to be taken on trust. Read the source, or open an issue if something looks wrong.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: If a future version starts doing something new with your data, this page gets updated before that version ships.
